title: Median and p90 delivery time per kitchen
prompt:
A dark-kitchen delivery service stores when each order was placed and when it was delivered. delivered_at is NULL for orders that never arrived.

Averages are skewed by a few disastrous deliveries, so ops wants the median and the 90th percentile of delivery time per kitchen, in minutes.

- Columns: kitchen, delivered, median_minutes, p90_minutes
- delivered is the number of delivered orders; undelivered orders are ignored everywhere
- Percentiles are continuous (interpolated between values), rounded to 1 decimal place
- Only kitchens with at least 3 delivered orders
- Order by median_minutes ascending, then kitchen ascending
hints: Delivery time in minutes is extract(epoch FROM delivered_at - ordered_at) / 60. What happens to it when delivered_at is NULL?
percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...) is an ordered-set aggregate that interpolates and skips NULLs. The 3-order rule must count delivered rows, not all rows.
round(percentile_cont(0.9) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY mins)::numeric, 1), with GROUP BY kitchen HAVING count(delivered_at) >= 3 ORDER BY median_minutes, kitchen.

exercise.schema: CREATE TABLE deliveries (id int PRIMARY KEY, kitchen text NOT NULL, ordered_at timestamp NOT NULL, delivered_at timestamp);
exercise.starter:
-- Delivery time percentiles per kitchen
SELECT kitchen,
       count(*) AS delivered,
       round(avg(extract(epoch FROM delivered_at - ordered_at) / 60), 1) AS median_minutes,
       round(max(extract(epoch FROM delivered_at - ordered_at) / 60), 1) AS p90_minutes
FROM deliveries
GROUP BY kitchen
HAVING count(*) >= 3
ORDER BY median_minutes, kitchen;
exercise.solution:
WITH timed AS (
  SELECT kitchen, extract(epoch FROM delivered_at - ordered_at) / 60 AS mins
  FROM deliveries
  WHERE delivered_at IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT kitchen,
       count(*) AS delivered,
       round(percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY mins)::numeric, 1) AS median_minutes,
       round(percentile_cont(0.9) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY mins)::numeric, 1) AS p90_minutes
FROM timed
GROUP BY kitchen
HAVING count(*) >= 3
ORDER BY median_minutes, kitchen;

hiddenTests.name: equal medians sorted by kitchen, fractional minutes
exactly three delivered among many rows

explanation: percentile_cont sorts each group's values and interpolates: with n values the p-th percentile sits at position p × (n − 1) counting from 0, so the median of 10, 20, 30, 100 is 25 and the p90 is 30 + 0.7 × 70 = 79. Filtering out undelivered orders first makes both the percentiles and the at-least-3 rule use delivered orders only; HAVING count(*) on the raw table is the trap that lets a kitchen with two deliveries and one lost order through. avg is not a median and is pulled up by outliers, and percentile_disc would return an actual value instead of interpolating. percentile_cont returns double precision, so cast to numeric before round(x, 1).
notes: Ordered-set aggregates sort each group, so cost is O(n log n) per kitchen and they cannot use hash aggregation; for huge tables an approximate sketch (t-digest, or pre-bucketed histograms) is common. You can ask for several percentiles in one sort with percentile_cont(ARRAY[0.5, 0.9]) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY mins), which returns an array. Percentiles cannot be added across groups, so a daily median cannot be rolled up into a monthly one without the raw rows.
followUps: Return both percentiles from a single percentile_cont call using an array argument.
